# bugs #4226: Numeric escape sequences of 0x80 and above in u, U, and L string literals give wrong elements or stop the compiler

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/4226/
- Category: [Fixes that need a decision](../../fix-decision.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17228
- Recommended action: Apply this patch or the second patch of the ticket's fourth comment, which was read and not built for this report. Then close.
- Patch: [bugs-4226.patch](../../patches/bugs-4226.patch), commit [`35996b568`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/35996b568c961994a59e5b4220dfb6612e9e03e8). Applies to r17228 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

On r17228 for mcs51, the first element of `u"\x100"` is 0, as the ticket reports for z80. Values
from 0x80 to 0xff give wrong results too. The first element of `u"\x80"` is 0. For `U"\xff"` the
compiler stops with an internal error from `wassert (seqlen <= 6)` in `src/SDCCutil.c`, and for
`L"\xe9"` it ends with SIGSEGV.

## Cause

`strVal()` in `src/SDCCval.c` converts the source of a `u`, `U`, or `L` literal to bytes with
`copyStrWithEscapeLimit()`, and then it decodes the bytes as UTF-8 with `utf_32_from_utf_8()`.
`copyStrWithEscapeLimit()` stores each numeric escape sequence as one byte, so values above 0xff
lose their upper bits. `utf_32_from_utf_8()` decodes the bytes from 0x80 to 0xff as bytes of
multi-byte sequences. For 0xff it computes a sequence length above 6, which its `wassert`
rejects. For 0xe9 the sequence has three bytes, and the function reads past the end of the
buffer.

## Fix

The new function `copyStr32()` in `src/SDCCutil.c` converts the source of a wide string literal
to 32-bit elements. It stores the value of each numeric escape sequence as one element, after the
range check of `escapeValueInRange()`, and it decodes only the characters between escape
sequences as UTF-8. `strVal()` calls it for `u`, `U`, and `L` literals. Byte strings and inline
assembly are converted by `copyStrWithEscapeLimit()`, which the patch does not change.

The patch changes the two conversion functions. `utf_16_from_utf_32()` stores every value up to
0xffff as one code unit. On r17228 its `wassert` fails for the surrogate values, which numeric
escape sequences can have, and for 0xd7ff. `utf_32_from_utf_8()` stops at the end of its input
when the last sequence is incomplete, because `copyStr32()` passes it the characters between two
escape sequences, and more of the literal follows them.

## Decision

The ticket has two patches from the reporter. The first is in trunk as r17136. The second, in the
fourth comment, is not in r17228, and a maintainer wrote in the fifth comment that a review will
follow. It was read for this entry and was not built. The maintainers choose between it and this
patch.

- Both patches store each numeric escape sequence as one 32-bit element, and both change the
  condition of `utf_16_from_utf_32()` to `codepoint <= 0xffff`. A numeric escape sequence with a
  surrogate value is then one code unit of a `u` literal.
- The reporter's patch gives the loop of `copyStrWithEscapeLimit()` a parameter for the size of
  the elements, and that loop converts byte strings and wide strings. This patch adds a separate
  function of about 40 lines for wide strings.
- The reporter's patch calls `utf_32_from_utf_8()` for the characters between two escape
  sequences, as this patch does, and it does not change that function.
- Each patch adds `support/regression/tests/bug-4226.c`. The reporter's file has cases for the
  delimited escape sequences of C2y and for byte strings, which the file of this patch does not
  have.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/bug-4226.c` has four functions and 62 assertions on `u`, `U`, and `L`
literals. They have hexadecimal and octal escape sequences with values up to 0xffffffff, among
them surrogate values and 0, beside characters of the source and universal character names. One
function has adjacent literals and an array with automatic storage duration. On r17228 the
compiler stops with an internal error for this file. With the patch the test passes on host,
stm8, ucz80, and six mcs51 variants, which are the four models and `--stack-auto` with the small
and large models.

With the patches of this report, the regression suite has 0 failures for host, mcs51-small,
mcs51-medium, mcs51-large, mcs51-huge, mcs51-small-stack-auto, mcs51-large-stack-auto, stm8, and
ucz80, and the diagnostics suite has 0 failures for mcs51, mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80,
and stm8.

## Related

- #4179 is about the range check of numeric escape sequences. Its fix,
  [r17124](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/17124/), added `parseEscape()` and
  `escapeValueInRange()`, which `copyStr32()` calls.
- `utf_16_from_utf_32()` subtracts 0x100000 from code points above 0xffff, and 0x10000 is
  correct. With the patch, `u"\U0001F600"` stops the compiler with an internal error from the
  `wassert` before the subtraction, and `u"\U0010FFFF"` gives 0xd83f 0xdfff, where 0xdbff 0xdfff
  is correct. The patch does not change these lines.
- A byte 0xff in the source of a wide string literal gives the internal error from
  `wassert (seqlen <= 6)` with and without the patch.
